    Explore the full training process +

    One word problem, from training example to answer.

    GSM8K · adapted training example

    48 clips in April. Half as many in May. How many in total?

    48 + 24 = 72 clips

    Scroll sideways to follow the full training map.

    PrepareStart with good examples

    Clean the data, remove duplicates, and keep evaluation questions separate from training.

    GSM8K example, shortened: 48 clips in April; half as many in May. Total?
    Learn languageFirst, learn how language works

    Turn broad text into tokens. Learn to predict the next piece of text, correcting mistakes over many batches.

    Toy text: “In April, she sold 48 …” → “clips”. Real pretraining uses a broad corpus, not this one math problem.
    Learn from examplesThen, learn how to answer

    Train on questions paired with worked answers. The model learns what a useful response looks like.

    May: 48 ÷ 2 = 24. Total: 48 + 24 = 72 clips.
    Optional branchSpecialize without retraining everything

    Optionally train small adapters on task-specific examples. LoRA is a way to fine-tune, not a required extra training stage.

    Use math question–answer pairs to practice explaining the two calculation steps.
    Alignment option AShow which answer is better

    One alignment option learns from preferred and rejected answers. These pairs must be created; GSM8K does not supply preference labels.

    Derived pair: “24 in May, 72 total” is preferred over the incorrect “96 total”.
    Alignment option BOr, learn from checked attempts

    Another option samples several solutions, scores them, and learns from their relative rewards. DPO and GRPO need not run one after the other.

    Illustrative attempts: 72, 96, 24, 72. A simple answer checker rewards 72; this is not a recorded model run.
    Check and improveTest on questions it has not studied

    Compare checkpoints on held-out questions. If results are poor, inspect the mistakes and revisit training. Never use test answers to train.

    The clips question above is training data. Evaluation uses a separate set of questions; no score is claimed here.
    Ready for inferenceSave a version people can use

    Save the chosen checkpoint and tokenizer, load them for inference, and check that the saved version behaves as expected.

    A user sends a new question → the model generates an answer → the answer is checked.

    Example adapted from GSM8K, first training item. Preference pairs and sampled attempts are illustrative. No model results are claimed.

    ChatMind · AI Agent System

    2025.12 – 2026.02

    Built a multi-step AI agent with tool calling and knowledge-base retrieval using pgvector, model switching, and streamed task progress via SSE.

    Java · Spring AI · PostgreSQL

    Explore the agent loop and architecture +

    Think → act → observe → adjust. Repeat until the task is answered or a limit is reached.

    Agent task loopResearch reference: 2026.09

    Scroll sideways to explore the full diagram.

    SetupLoad the guide and task

    The guide is indexed before the question. The agent receives its tools, model choice and available context.

    Task: Can I book Cedar for 90 minutes?
    Round 1 · decideRound 1: choose a search

    The model chooses a tool and a query. A first attempt can be too broad or point at the wrong section.

    Illustrative first query: “Cedar equipment”.
    Round 1 · actRound 1: run the tool

    KnowledgeTool searches the attached knowledge base. In this scripted example, the agent initially focuses on an equipment passage.

    Passage shown, not the full tool response: “Cedar has a display and a whiteboard.”
    Round 1 · not enoughNotice the missing information

    Tool results join the conversation. On the next model call, the agent can see that equipment does not answer a booking-duration question.

    Still missing: the maximum booking length. The task is not finished.
    Round 2 · revise and actRound 2: change the query

    Use the previous result to choose a better next action, rather than repeating the same search unchanged.

    New query: “Cedar meeting room booking policy”.
    Round 2 · evidence foundRound 2: use the new evidence

    Retrieve the booking policy and rerank the candidates. The returned text now answers the missing part.

    Observation: “Each booking may last at most 60 minutes.”
    Finish · supported answerFinish when the task is answered

    The model can now respond from the guide and terminate the task. The existing step limit also prevents an endless loop.

    Expected answer: No. Choose an available slot of 60 minutes or less.
    Return · progress + replyKeep the user informed throughout

    SSE delivers progress and generated messages during the loop. This highlight follows the return path to the browser.

    Two searches, one improved answer. This is a scripted illustration, not a recorded run.
    Proposed · baselineTurn a bad run into a test

    Keep the request, tool observations and expected outcome. The repository has retrieval evaluation; full trajectory replay is an extension.

    Failure fixture: an answer allows 90 minutes even though the guide says 60.
    Proposed · revise contextImprove what each step sees

    Retrieve the relevant context and discover tools only when needed. Existing memory compression is a starting point; dynamic tool discovery is an extension.

    Give the next attempt the booking policy, not a pile of unrelated tool descriptions.
    Proposed · durable harnessMake long tasks recoverable

    Save execution checkpoints and isolate tools. On interruption, restore progress and prevent repeated side effects; stored chat history alone is not enough.

    Resume after a stopped tool call without sending the same email twice.
    Proposed · optional workersUse specialists only when useful

    A coordinator can split independent research tasks and combine concise results. A single room-policy lookup does not need extra agents.

    For a larger comparison, one worker reads policy while another checks a separate guide.
    Proposed · check outcomeCheck against external evidence

    An independent verifier checks the answer against the guide and explicit success criteria, instead of trusting the agent’s confidence.

    Checks: limit = 60; reject 90; identify the policy; do not claim a room was booked.
    Proposed · engineering iterationRevise, rerun, and compare

    Change the prompt, context or tool handling. Replay the failure and regression cases; keep the candidate only if it improves the measured outcomes.

    Baseline → revised harness → replay → compare. If it still fails, revise again. Model weights do not change in this loop.

    Solid modules: repository capabilities. Amber dashed modules: proposed extensions. The two-round story is illustrative; model decisions and retrieval results vary.

    Engineering references · 2026.09 +

    Selected current engineering patterns, not a benchmark ranking. These references inform the proposed extensions; they do not establish that ChatMind implements them.

    • Harness design (2026.03): separate execution from evaluation and use feedback to revise the system.
    • LangGraph persistence and managed-agent architecture (2026.04): checkpoints, recoverable state and separated execution environments.
    • Advanced tool use (2025.11): discover relevant tools on demand.
    • Agent evaluations (2026.01): inspect trajectories and grade real outcomes.
    • Multi-agent research (2025.06): use specialist delegation for tasks that benefit from independent work.
